CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual examination.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc who presents for annual examination.

Regarding her herniated disc, the patient reports it has been doing well since receiving a steroid injection several months ago. She currently denies any back pain or limitations in movement.

For her prior carpal tunnel release, performed a couple of years ago, the patient reports she has returned to work without any recurrent issues. She denies numbness or tingling in her hands and has maintained full range of motion.

Regarding her coronary artery disease, the patient reports experiencing chest pain over the past month. The chest pain occurs with exertion (walking) and resolves with rest. She denies experiencing chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest, occurring approximately three times per week. She does not feel it is concerning enough to warrant emergency department evaluation. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pressure/pain and nasal congestion related to seasonal allergies. Negative for shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, and chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
2. Prior carpal tunnel release
3. Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
1. Aspirin
2. Toprol

ALLERGIES
Environmental allergies (pollen).

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is employed and currently working.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygen saturation normal.
Heart: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated (previously noted).
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neck: No carotid bruits appreciated.
Extremities: No lower extremity edema. Healed surgical scars noted on right wrist.

RESULTS
Echocardiogram (prior year): Ejection fraction 45% (mildly reduced). Mild mitral regurgitation noted.
ECG: Stable, consistent with prior coronary artery disease. No new changes.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release status post: Patient is doing well with no recurrent symptoms. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient instructed to report if symptoms recur.

2. Herniated disc: Patient is doing well following prior steroid injection with minimal symptoms. No further steroid injection or physical therapy indicated at this time. Patient instructed to report if symptoms recur.

3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: This is the most concerning problem identified. Continue aspirin and Toprol. Stress test ordered to evaluate for additional coronary blockages. Lipid panel ordered. Crestor 20 mg once daily initiated. Nursing will assist with scheduling of tests and follow-up.
